release.note: Prepare the first beta, 0.1.0-beta.1 with Android code 13, retain the existing signing certificate and documentation epoch, align release commands, and describe the remaining prerelease and native qualification limits. Generated publication notes now describe a prerelease rather than an alpha.

configuration.note: Align the default app and Zero image pair with beta.1 in the packaged guides. This release changes image versions, not operator settings or the retained credentials required for upgrades.

deployment.note: Align chart metadata, resource labels and packaged deployment image examples with 0.1.0-beta.1. Preserve app/Zero pairing, storage and recovery guidance, and cluster qualification limits; the optional one-image bundle remains separate from standard release assets.

native.note: Document native export source labels and upload times, separate system save dialogs, retained prepared files after cancellation or save failure, and Saved only after a confirmed write. Document Android Back dismissal and navigation order, top-level exit, and background network teardown during Activity recreation. Document recovery-code downloads through account-bound native save operations on Android and desktop, retry after a failed write, and distinct Android connection diagnostics without relaxing certificate trust. Document localized keyring setup and retry, the Linux package recommendation, and account-bound fixed Settings browser handoffs on desktop and Android. Matching Settings routes preserve the destination through browser sign-in; older servers still open their normal application page. Document the desktop online-start requirement for cached data, retry after reconnection, retention of durably saved edits, and the remaining encrypted evidence and refusal-policy work in issue 1090. Android cached activation and native credential and trust checks are unchanged. Document the asynchronous five-second launcher wait, retryable spawn and non-zero exit failures, and successful handoff when a launcher remains running beyond the bound.

authentication.note: OAuth registration denials preserve their stable policy code through Better Auth callback redirects. Native browser sign-in retains the grant ID and displays the localized policy message. Document periodic stream revalidation after session revocation; HTTP authorization remains checked against live session state. Invitations remain HTTPS browser links with fragment tokens and backward-compatible acceptance; native task scheme handling is unchanged.

compatibility.note: Document restricted-role membership removal without TEMP and uniform 404 attachment denials, with unchanged persisted formats. Attachment garbage collection uses the same checked-out connection as its leader lock. Persisted attachment states, ciphertext format, quotas and restore procedures are unchanged.
compatibility.upgrade: Deploy the application update without schema, blob or key conversion; runtime TEMP grants are unnecessary. No schema or ciphertext migration is required; restart the application with the updated image.
compatibility.backup: Keep the existing coordinated database and blob backups; ciphertext and key envelopes are unchanged. The existing database and attachment backup procedure remains applicable without changes.
compatibility.rollback: The previous application remains data-compatible but restores the TEMP dependency and foreign attachment 403 response. The prior application can use the same database and attachment objects; no format changes occur.
compatibility.clientVersions: Existing web, Android and desktop clients use unchanged attachment formats and interpret unauthorized downloads as unavailable. Browser, Android and desktop clients use the same attachment protocol and remain compatible.
